This vignette records what we learned before converting `ttdviewer` from a `bslib` UI to [`shinyreact`](https://posit-dev.github.io/shinyreact/). We built a small prototype (a spike) to test the pieces the `shinyreact` documentation does not cover, and every piece worked. The code below is shown but not run, so building this vignette does not require `shinyreact`.

## What `shinyreact` is

`shinyreact` moves the UI out of R. The server still holds the reactive graph (`input`, `reactive()`, `req()`, `bindEvent()` all behave as usual), but the page is a React client we write ourselves. `shinyreact` ships the plumbing between the two and no UI components.

The R package is version 0.1.0 and the documentation calls it pre-release. It is not on CRAN:

```{r}
#| eval: false
pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r")
```

The spike used GitHub commit `42c500f`.



## R side

The R package exports seven functions:

```{r}
#| eval: false
ls("package:shinyreact")
#> [1] "page_bare"       "page_react"      "page_react_dep"  "page_react_html"
#> [5] "reactive_output" "send_message"    "wire_tap"
```

`page_react()` replaces the UI function. It serves `ui.js` (and `ui.css`, if present) from `src_dir`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
args(shinyreact::page_react)
#> function (..., src_dir = "www", js_file = "ui.js", css_file = "ui.css",
#>     title = NULL, lang = "en", shinyreact_js = "server")
```

`reactive_output()` sends any R value to the client as JSON:

```{r}
#| eval: false
output$titles <- shinyreact::reactive_output(
  sort(unique(all_tt_combined$title))
)
```

## Client side

The client reads and writes Shiny values with hooks on `window.shinyreact`:

* `useShinyInput(id, default)`: returns `[value, setValue]` and sets `input[[id]]` on the server.
* `useShinyOutputValue(id, default)`: the value from a `reactive_output()`.
* `useShinyOutputStatus(id)`: `"pending"`, `"ready"`, `"recalculating"`, or `"error"`.
* `useShinyInitialized()` and `useShinyBusy()`: connection and busy state (a replacement for `useBusyIndicators()`).
* `ShinyOutput`: hosts a classic Shiny output (any output binding) inside React.
* `ImageOutput`: hosts a `renderPlot()` image.
* `ShinyModuleProvider`: namespaces hook ids, for Shiny modules.

## What the spike tested

The documentation shows R examples only for `plotly` and `reactable`. It says nothing about `listviewerlite`, `renderPlot()`, `downloadHandler()`, or packaging the client inside an installed R package. Those are four of the app's five outputs, so the spike tested each one with Netflix Titles (one file) and Space Launches (two files).

### Lists

`listviewerlite::listview()` returns HTML, so the server keeps `renderUI()` and the client hosts it with the `shiny-html-output` class:

```{r}
#| eval: false
output$list <- renderUI({
  req(data())
  listviewerlite::listview(data())
})
```

```js
h(ShinyOutput, { id: "list", className: "shiny-html-output" })
```

### Tables

`reactable` works the documented way. `shinyreact` finds the widget's JavaScript from the render function, so no `reactableOutput()` placeholder is needed:

```{r}
#| eval: false
output$table <- reactable::renderReactable({
  req(data())
  reactable::reactable(utils::head(data()[[1]], 1000), searchable = TRUE)
})
```

```js
h(ShinyOutput, {
  id: "table",
  className: "reactable html-widget html-widget-output",
  "data-reactable-output": "table"
})
```

### Plots

`ImageOutput` is documented for Python only, but it follows the same contract as R's `renderPlot()`. The client reports its size through `.clientdata_output_<id>_width` and `_height`, and draws the `src` that `renderPlot()` returns. The `inspect_plot()` ggplots rendered unchanged:

```{r}
#| eval: false
output$plt_types <- renderPlot({
  req(data())
  inspect_plot(data()[1], plots = "types")
})
```

```js
h(ImageOutput, { id: "plt_types", width: "100%", height: "300px" })
```

### Downloads

`downloadHandler()` binds to an anchor with the `shiny-download-link` class, so `ShinyOutput` with `tagName: "a"` works. The CSV download returned 3.0 MB, and the two file zip returned 104 KB:

```{r}
#| eval: false
output$download <- downloadHandler(
  filename = function() tt_download_filename(data(), input$format, input$title),
  content = function(file) write_tt_download(data(), input$format, file)
)
```

```js
h(ShinyOutput, {
  id: "download", tagName: "a", className: "btn shiny-download-link",
  href: "", target: "_blank", download: ""
}, "Download")
```

### Packaging

`page_react()` passes `src_dir` to `page_react_dep()`, which builds an `htmltools::htmlDependency()` with a file source. A file source works from an installed package, so the built client belongs in `inst/www/`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
app_ui <- function() {
  shinyreact::page_react(
    src_dir = system.file("www", package = "ttdviewer"),
    title = "ttdviewer"
  )
}
```

An installed build serves `ui.js` from `ttdviewer/www/` (checked with `R CMD INSTALL` into a temporary library).

## Gotcha: length one vectors

`reactive_output()` serializes with `auto_unbox`, so a character vector of length one arrives as a string, not an array. The spike crashed on `files.names.join()` for a dataset with one file. Either wrap on the client or protect the vector on the server:

```js
[].concat(files.names).join(", ")
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
list(names = I(names(d)))
```

## The conversion

The conversion followed the spike:

* Client: `js/` holds a Vite and TSX project (`npm run build`) that writes `inst/www/ui.js` and `ui.css`. JSX compiles to `React.createElement`, and Vite maps `react` to the global `shinyreact.React`, so the bundle carries no copy of React. `js/` is in `.Rbuildignore`; the built bundle is committed, so installing the package needs no Node.
* `app_ui()`: calls `page_react()` with `theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5)` (so the client can use Bootstrap classes) and `useBusyIndicators()`.
* Modules: the `mod_*_ui()` functions are gone. Each server module keeps its id; the client wraps each component in a `ShinyModuleProvider` with the same namespace. Plain values (titles, file names, the file overview) moved to `reactive_output()`.
* `mod_plot_server()`: one `renderPlot()` per plot type, each gated by `req(plt %in% input$plots)`, in place of `renderUI()` and an observer.

| Module | R output | Client |
|---|---|---|
| `mod_input` | `titles` (`reactive_output()`) | `TitleInput.tsx` |
| `mod_download` | `files` (`reactive_output()`); `download` (`downloadHandler()`) | `Download.tsx` |
| `mod_list` | `list` (`renderUI()`) | `ListTab.tsx` |
| `mod_summary` | `overview`, `choices` (`reactive_output()`); `stats`, `vars`, `table` (`renderReactable()`) | `SummaryTab.tsx` |
| `mod_plot` | `datasets` (`reactive_output()`); `plt_<type>` (`renderPlot()`) | `GraphsTab.tsx` |

One surprise: `output$dev` (the `app_server()` reactive values panel) errored at startup. Inside a closed `<details>` in bslib it was never rendered; inside React it is, and `listviewerlite::listview()` fails on `NULL` elements. It now drops them with `purrr::compact()`.
